title: Flatness descends through a faithfully flat module
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $M$ be an $S$-module. If $M$ is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and faithfully flat as an $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], then $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Let $u:N_1\to N_2$ be an injective $R$-linear map. By the definition of a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] it suffices to show that $u\otimes1_S:N_1\otimes_RS\to N_2\otimes_RS$ is injective; by the symmetry isomorphisms $N_i\otimes_RS\cong S\otimes_RN_i$, $n\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes n$, which commute with $u\otimes1_S$ and $1_S\otimes u$, it is equivalent to show that $1_S\otimes u:S\otimes_RN_1\to S\otimes_RN_2$ is injective. (Stacks argues with an exact sequence $N_1\to N_2\to N_3$; with the definition of flatness used here, by injective maps, the case $0\to N_1\to N_2$ is the one needed.)

$M$ is a flat $R$-module (via $R\to S$), so by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] $u\otimes1_M:N_1\otimes_RM\to N_2\otimes_RM$ is injective, hence, composing with the symmetry isomorphisms $N_i\otimes_RM\cong M\otimes_RN_i$, so is $1_M\otimes_Ru:M\otimes_RN_1\to M\otimes_RN_2$.

(Stacks: 'we may write this as $N_i\otimes_RS\otimes_SM$'.) By the natural isomorphisms $c_{N_i}:M\otimes_S(S\otimes_RN_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_RN_i$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-cancel-base-change], $(1_M\otimes_Ru)\circ c_{N_1}=c_{N_2}\circ(1_M\otimes_S(1_S\otimes u))$, so $1_M\otimes_S(1_S\otimes u)=c_{N_2}^{-1}\circ(1_M\otimes_Ru)\circ c_{N_1}$ is injective by step 2.

Consider the complex of $S$-modules $0\to S\otimes_RN_1\xrightarrow{1_S\otimes u}S\otimes_RN_2$ (composite zero). Applying $M\otimes_S-$ gives $0=M\otimes_S0\to M\otimes_S(S\otimes_RN_1)\to M\otimes_S(S\otimes_RN_2)$, which is exact by step 3. As $M$ is a faithfully flat $S$-module, the definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] (a complex is exact if and only if its tensor product with $M$ is) shows that $0\to S\otimes_RN_1\to S\otimes_RN_2$ is exact, i.e. $1_S\otimes u$ is injective. By step 1, $R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 039V (algebra.tex 8958-8978). Statement kept. Proof written in four steps from the Stacks proof, restricted to injections 0 -> N1 -> N2 because def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map defines flatness by injective maps; the DAG's faithfully-flat definition is the exactness-reflecting one (00HB(2)), so injectivity of 1_S (x) u follows directly by applying it to the complex 0 -> S(x)N1 -> S(x)N2 (no derivation from 'N (x) M = 0 => N = 0' needed). The identification 'N_i (x)_R S (x)_S M = N_i (x)_R M' that Stacks writes without comment became the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-cancel-base-change (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange with naturality lTensor_comp_cancelBaseChange); the existing lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-transitive is only the case M = T a ring and lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change only the algebra case, so neither covers an arbitrary S-module M. No Mathlib match for the item itself (searches recorded). Citer lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence uses it with R=A, S=B, M=C, which fits the statement.
